facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 金_偏财 (Metal carrying The Horizon). Persona The Horizon (偏财). Definition line: "Wide-ranging engagement, opportunity sensed at a distance". Keyword Reach, charge dynamic, poles catalyst Momentum / friction Scatter. Family function: Action. Cost dimension: opportunity sensed far off; the near things blur. Arena: horizon, wind, open road, far light, the next place. Classical portrait: wide-ranging engagement; opportunity sensed at a distance; windfall, generosity, the near things blur. Ruled domains: Opportunity, Ventures, Father. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 正财.
Element arena: Metal (edge, blade, ore, forge, whetstone, the clean line). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Fire. structural_interaction seed: "Fire directing Metal broadly — warmth applied to precision as distributed material".
- k2_overview: "Your Metal moves as the Horizon: an edge pointed outward. You mint opportunity, spotting value with an assayer’s eye and striking while metal is hot. Deals sharpen you, markets read like open books, and money is a tool you handle without trembling. Fortune favors your precision. Fence one treasury it cannot touch."
- k2_functional: "You strike opportunities with timing others envy: measured approach, decisive cut."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Quick-eyed","Polished","Adventurous"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Opportunity":"You see openings as clearly as flaws in ore: the undervalued asset, the mispriced moment. Trust the eye and audit the appetite. Two ventures cut deep beat ten scratched shallow.","Ventures":"Your ventures favor precision plays: quality arbitrage, timing trades, craft turned to commerce. Structure each like a blade, defined edge, clean handle, known length, and your record stays enviable.","Father":"The father-thread in your chart carries metal: a paternal figure of standards, trade, or discipline whose mark shows in how you value things. Settle those accounts. Honor or forgiveness both count as payment."}
- fn_reading.friction.ledger (three rows, index-aligned to adj_chips.friction; authored order is significance order):
  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 金_正财 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Thorough","Trustworthy","Slow and steady"],"friction":["No-frills","Greedy","Won’t budge"]}
- Sibling cell 金_正财 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Comfort gets audited out of your life on principle. The heating conservative, the furnishings functional, the pleasures budgeted to their nutritional minimum: discipline built the estate, and somewhere it kept building past the point of purpose, into corners nobody warms."

Core element Fire, energy element Metal. Law: Fire tames Metal (火克金: the forge softens the blade). Relative to the core the energy is the tamed, so Metal is this core's Action. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Fire core that shows Metal on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Metal as the Action is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 火_金's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: The move you trust most is moving on. You need the next place in view to feel free, so you move on at the first slow week rather than stay. You walk away from what each venture cost you to start.

value_b.text: You are always moving on, and the moving feels like being alive. You feel staying long enough to be known is giving up, and you move on ahead of the finish. Remember that moving on costs you the one thing you had started to build.

value.text: Always moving on is how you avoid being pinned. You would rather move on to somewhere new than be found at the old venture, even with money still in it. You leave more money behind by moving on than new ventures bring in.

value.text: Moving on, you leave people as well as plans. You move on and put the next place ahead of those who built the last one with you. Each time you move on, you leave your partners starting over.

value.text: Spread thin is how you like it. You feel most at ease with several ventures open, and you spread yourself across all of them rather than into one. You end up thin in the one place you most wanted to go deep.

value_b.text: You spread yourself thin on purpose. You know a single venture would ask for all you have, so you spread yourself over a handful rather than wholly into one. Do not forget that thin shares of you add up to less than one whole one.

value.text: Spread thin, you never learn what you could do whole. You stay spread over shallow ventures rather than deep in one, since the one you skipped always looks better. Spread thin, you pay in rest never taken and the one venture that would have paid.

value.text: Spending it all is your first instinct. You feel money that sits is a chance going cold, and you spend it all on the next thing rather than keep it. Remember that you are allowed to let money sit until the right chance comes.

value_b.text: You spend it all because it came easily. You feel keeping money is admitting the next windfall is not coming, so you spend it rather than protect against that. Hold on to the fact that you spend the windfall faster than you earn the wage.

value.text: Deciding what to keep is harder than spending it all. You spend to feel money move rather than sit, since a sum held still feels like a missed chance. Spent out, you come up short for the one opening that asks for cash up front.

value.text: Where you are generous, you spend everything too. You spend it on the bill, the gift and the loan, since giving suits you better than keeping. You spend the money your family was counting on for later.
